Northern Kentucky Economic Prosperity Index

Northern Kentucky’s economy is usually reported as part of the Cincinnati metro, which hides how Boone, Kenton, and Campbell counties are doing on their own. This index measures the three counties together against every U.S. metro of 250,000+ residents, giving funders, partners, and policymakers one consistent picture of where the region leads, where it lags, and whether it is moving in the right direction.

Use the to see every metro at once, or to line Northern Kentucky up against any peer.

Goals

BE NKY Growth Partnership has identified these eight goals as the priorities where progress by 2030 will do the most to raise prosperity for Northern Kentucky residents and strengthen the region’s competitiveness with metros across the country. Together they cover growth, wages and income, workforce participation, entrepreneurship, high-value industries, talent, and affordability.

Each goal is a value to reach by 2030, tracked against a straight path from 2019.

How goals are tracked
  • GRP per capita is the region’s GDP divided by its population, in current dollars.
  • Every goal is a set value chosen by the Partnership.
  • Dollar goals are in current dollars, so part of the progress toward them will come from inflation.
  • The path runs in a straight line from the 2019 value to the goal in 2030. On track means the latest value is at or ahead of the path, allowing a small margin. Met means the goal value is already reached.

      How the scores work
      • Each metric is converted to a z-score against the benchmark metros (lower-is-better metrics are flipped), capped at ±3. Dollar and skewed metrics use a log scale.
      • Domain scores average their metric z-scores and are re-standardized; the overall score averages all metric z-scores and needs at least 5 of 6 domains.
      • Metric scores place each metric’s z-score on a bell curve and scale it to 0 to 10, so a small difference in value moves the score only a little, even where many metros are bunched together. Domain and overall scores are the share of benchmark metros a region outperforms, times 10. Northern Kentucky is scored against the metros but is not part of the benchmark, since its counties sit inside the Cincinnati MSA.
      • "Latest" uses each region's most recent value per metric (mostly 2024, with several reaching 2025). Single years (2015 to 2024) re-score every region on that year's data. Regions are built from member counties (2023 OMB delineations).
      Source: BE NKY Growth Partnership. Data from the Census Bureau, BEA, BLS, USPTO PatentsView, the Stanford Education Data Archive, and the USDA Forest Service.
